items.excerpt: Fresh from its Universal Music licensing deal, ElevenLabs has unveiled Music v2.5, the latest version of its AI music generation service - while stressing that UMG was not involved in this particular model.
Music Ally reads UMG's ElevenLabs tie-up as part of a bigger bet on official AI remix experiences, where fans get sanctioned tools to rework catalogue instead of prompting unlicensed models.

Global labels body IFPI used a Brussels event to press EU member states to fully implement the AI Act's training-data transparency rules, a fight that shapes what generative music tools may legally learn from.
Roger Taylor says a Queen avatar show is 'sort of' on the table, putting the ABBA Voyage template - digital doubles, motion capture and synthetic performance - back in front of legacy acts.
A former Spotify exec's studio ships experimental music-making 'singles' as small apps that deliberately avoid AI prompting, betting playful human interaction beats text-to-music generation.
Avid previewed a Pro Tools Stem Separator extension at IBC 2026 that splits a stereo mix into stems inside the session, pulling AI source separation into the pro post and mix workflow.
A working engineer's argument for where AI stops: models can generate and clean up audio, but taste, direction and the human calls in a session are what a producer is actually paid for.
With AI able to produce endless competent, listenable, boring music on demand, this essay argues the scarce asset is the 'human premium' - and maps how musicians can build their work around it.
Music Reports' Cuetrak now uses AudioShake-powered AI content recognition to build cue sheets automatically, taking one of the most tedious hand-logged jobs in music-for-picture off composers' desks.
Symphonic's Jorge Brea argues the real strain of AI music is operational: metadata, rights matching and delivery pipelines have to absorb an explosion of machine-made tracks.
A new class action skips copyright and accuses Suno of encoding musicians' identities into its model then exploiting them - a publicity-rights angle that could reshape AI voice and style mimicry.
The US DoJ has intervened to argue that AI training on copyrighted works is fair use - a position that lands directly on the music industry's cases against Suno and Udio.
Serato DJ 5.0's public beta rebuilds BPM and beatgrid analysis and widens streaming access, automating prep work DJs have historically done track by track.
Nopia is a compact chord-driven hardware instrument that generates harmony from gestures - a physical take on generative composition aimed at players who don't think in keyboards.
